extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent attorneys, and applicants (Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining novelty under the Korean Patent Act (Article 29), including what counts as prior art (publicly known/practiced, distributed publications, telecommunication disclosures), claim interpretation rules, and examiner procedures for citing prior art and handling disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (Article 29)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention having industrial applicability is patentable, other than inventions that (1) are publicly known or practiced prior to filing, or (2) are published in a distributed publication or made available to the public via telecommunication lines prior to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purport of the Patent System is to grant exclusive rights as a reward for disclosure; inventions already disclosed to the public shall not be granted exclusive rights. Prior to filing, inventions publicly known, publicly practiced, described in a publication, or made available via telecommunication lines do not involve novelty and are not patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must be industrially applicable to be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The principle does not mean an invention is industrially applicable solely because future technological advances could make it usable; industrial applicability must be present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: publicly known invention
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention the contents of which have been known to an unspecified person without obligation of secrecy in Korea or a foreign country prior to the filing of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time 'prior to the filing of the application' refers to the exact point in time (hour and minute) of filing (converted to Korean time). 'Unspecified persons' are the general public who do not have a duty of secrecy. Example: an application not laid open or published after registration is not prior art under Article 29(1)(2), though it may be prior art after public inspection under other provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: publicly practiced invention
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention which has been practiced under conditions where the contents are publicly known or can potentially be publicly known in Korea or a foreign country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parts of technical features remain secret in practice, the invention may not be considered publicly practiced. Conditions making an invention publicly practiced include situations where a skilled person can easily understand the invention by observing exposed manufacturing processes, or where inner parts can be observed/explained to visitors (e.g., plant tours where observation/explanation is not refused).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributed publication: what counts as a publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A publication is a document, drawing, or similar medium duplicated by printing, mechanical or chemical methods to disclose contents to the public through distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution means placing the publication where unspecified persons can read or see it; actual access by a particular person is not required. Patent gazettes on microfilm or CD-ROM, non-patent documents on floppy disks/slides/presentations or microfilm/CD-ROM produced to make contents available to the public are distributed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution: when a publication is 'distributed'
rubrics_metrics.description: Placing a publication so that unspecified persons can read or see it constitutes distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It does not require proof that any particular person actually accessed the publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of distribution: presumption rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When publication time is indicated, presumed dates are: (a) year only -> last day of that year; (b) month and year -> last day of that month; (c) full date -> that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where date not indicated: for foreign publications, presume distribution based on normal transit time to Korea if receipt date in Korea is clear; for derivative publications (reviews/extractions/catalogs) presume based on derivative's publication date; second editions presume first edition's date if contents accord; use other appropriate information to presume or estimate date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention described in a publication (essence vs literal)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention is considered described if the matters are described or 'essentially described,' i.e., directly derivable from what is described taking into account common general knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a utility innovation to be described, at least the configuration should be described. Mere photographs of interior technical features may not suffice. 'Essentially described' covers matters derivable by a skilled person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telecommunication-line disclosures recognized as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Technologies published over the Internet or other telecommunication lines can be considered prior art, reflecting public availability, propagation speed, and skill-level comparability to printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because internet content can be altered, care must be taken to determine date and content. The revised Patent Act (effective July 1, 2013) treats inventions made available over all telecommunication lines as prior art under Article 29(1)(ii). Previously only lines 'designated by Presidential Decree' had that status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment by application date for telecommunication disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Different rules apply to applications filed before June 30, 2013 and those filed after July 1, 2013 regarding how telecommunication disclosures are cited as prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For filings before June 30, 2013, only disclosures via telecommunication lines designated by Presidential Decree are treated as publication-equivalent prior art (Article 29(1)(ii)); other telecommunication disclosures may be cited under publicly known/practiced (Article 29(1)(i)). For filings after July 1, 2013 all telecommunication disclosures are cited under Article 29(1)(ii). The technical criteria for determining which telecommunication lines can confirm disclosure content/time are the same regardless of application date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telecommunication line: definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A telecommunication line includes public bulletin boards, e-mail groups, internet, and future electronic/telecommunication methods; it covers transmission/reception of code, words, sound or image through wired, wireless, optical or other electromagnetic processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures via CD-ROM or diskette are not telecommunication-line disclosures but distributed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability to the public via telecommunication lines
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Available to the public' means the invention can be seen by an unspecified person; actual access is not required. If access is restricted to specific persons, it is not available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether information is on a website accessible by general search engines or encoded so it cannot generally be read. Only inventions 'available to the public' can be cited as prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telecommunication lines designated under Enforcement Decree — reliable operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the revision, telecommunication lines operated by governments, national/public schools/universities, national/public research institutes, or corporations designated and publicly notified by the KIPO Commissioner were deemed to have the status of publication-equivalent prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: KIPO's cyber bulletin; designated organizations include KIPA and Korea Institute of Patent Information. International intergovernmental organizations (UN, WIPO, WTO, EPO, etc.) count; NGOs generally do not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of disclosure content and disclosure time (examiner credibility evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because website content can be updated or altered, the examiner must present evidence that the prior art was disclosed at the indicated date and must review credibility based on the type of telecommunication line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the line is one of the designated/reliable types, the examiner may accept content/time without extra confirmation. For other lines the examiner must evaluate public awareness, use frequency, operator credibility, operation period, etc. If credibility is doubtful, the examiner should seek confirmation (e.g., ask the operator or use Internet Archive www.archive.org). If doubts persist, the disclosure may only be cited when actual disclosure date is confirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of citation for electronic technical information
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing electronic technical information from telecommunication lines, list bibliographic items (author, title, publication name, pages/drawings/graphs) in compliance with WIPO Standards ST.14, as far as known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If cited documentation is a patent published online, the examiner may describe it in the same manner as patent official gazettes (e.g., CD-ROM form) without needing to record search date and website address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters requiring attention: hyper-linked websites
rubrics_metrics.description: Websites hyper-linked from reliable telecommunication lines are not automatically considered to be the same reliable lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyperlinked sites' credibility regarding time of disclosure cannot be guaranteed because they are run by other entities; do not treat them as designated/reliable telecommunication lines without separate credibility assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination instructions summary for telecommunication disclosures (table mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary mapping showing how disclosures through various telecommunication lines are cited depending on whether the application was filed before June 30, 2013 or after July 1, 2013 and depending on credibility/confirmation of disclosure date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., disclosures through lines under Article 1-2 before revision => cited as Article 29(1)(ii) prior art for both filing periods; disclosures through other lines where credibility recognized or date confirmed => for pre-revision filings cited as Article 29(1)(i), for post-revision cited as Article 29(1)(ii); where credibility is in doubt => not cited as prior art (pre-revision) or not cited (post-revision) unless date confirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination when applicant contests telecommunication disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant raises opposition about accessibility, content, or disclosure time of a telecommunication-line disclosure, the examiner must consider the applicant's evidence and seek additional evidence to confirm the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner cannot find confirming evidence, the invention disclosed on the telecommunication line cannot be cited as prior art. Mere applicant assertions that the line is unreliable without specific evidence do not oblige the examiner to accept them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of novelty (general procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner determines novelty by judging whether the claimed invention falls under the inventions categorized in Article 29(1)(1) to (2). If it does, it is not novel; if it does not, it is novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must describe the subject matter sought for protection (Article 42(4)). Determination of identicalness is based on matters described in the claims. When multiple claims exist, novelty must be determined for each claim separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining inventions disclosed in claims — clear claim language
rubrics_metrics.description: When claim language is clear, the claimed invention should be defined as recited in the claim. Terminology in claims is interpreted with the general meaning accepted in the technical field, except where a specific meaning is explicitly defined in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation should be objective and reasonable, considering technical meaning and a person skilled in the art at filing time. Example: 'cream' in claims should not be limited to a specific embodiment described in the description if 'cream' has its general meaning in the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid limiting claims by referencing description or drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the claim description is clearly understood, an examiner should avoid limiting interpretation merely by referencing the description or drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters described only in the description or drawings and not in the claims should be considered not recited in the claims. Conversely, matters recited in the claims should be considered even if not in the description. Examples: do not limit 'thin film type probe' to patterns shown only in the drawings; do not import rotation direction from drawings if not recited in claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific definitions in the description control only if clearly specified
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant specifically defines a term in the description to make it different from its general meaning, the term should be interpreted with that specific meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, mere disclosure of a specific concept of a term in the description and drawings does not by itself constitute a specific definition. A term should be unified over the whole specification and is interpreted in its general technical-field meaning unless a clear specific definition is intended and evident.
